links.outcome: Effect of recalibration methods on model performance in shifted target datasets versus uncalibrated predictions
links.effect: SFI-aware calibration improved F1 by +4.2% to +34.9% and AUC by +4.7% to +40.1%; isotonic regression degraded AUC to 0.51-0.56; Platt scaling effects were inconsistent.
links.quote: Traditional methods treat all predictions equivalently, applying uniform calibration adjustments regardless of underlying data quality.

links.outcome: Performance degradation of uncalibrated models when deployed across datasets differing in demographics and data quality
links.effect: Uncalibrated random forest models showed modest performance (e.g., dementia F1 0.395, AUC 0.723) on shifted test datasets; SFI-aware calibration lifted dementia F1 to 0.533.
links.quote: Machine learning models trained on real-world data (RWD) often experience performance degradation when deployed across different settings due to distributional shift.

unlisted_practices: Patient-level data-fidelity index (Signal Fidelity Index) used for label-free post-hoc calibration under distributional shift

links.outcome: F1 and AUC under heterogeneous target datasets
links.effect: F1 +4.2% to +34.9% and AUC +4.6 % to +40% versus uncalibrated predictions and baselines.
links.quote: Evaluation across six phenotypes and 3,550 synthetic datasets demonstrated consistent performance improvements (F1 score +4.2% to +34.9%, AUC +4.6 % to +40%) over uncalibrated predictions and established baseline methods.

links.effect: ECE decreased in five phenotypes (−45.2% to −3.5%) but increased +7.7% for adult ADHD.
links.quote: Notably, ECE decreased for several phenotypes–indicating improved bin-level calibration–(hypertension: –45.2%, geriatric bipolar: –22.7%, type 2 diabetes: –15.4%, dementia: –14.2%, fibromyalgia: –3.5%), while adult ADHD showed a modest ECE increase (+7.7%).

unlisted_practices: Patient-level diagnostic fidelity calibration using structured EHR metadata
